mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 6 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces the cost of capital and increases equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS has declined over the past 6 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.2 percentage points from the previous month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp from prior month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in demand, which signals an impending economic slowdown and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline from the prior month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of rising industrial production (INDPRO) growth, the economy is in an expansion phase, which boosts corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO rises > 0.1% from prior month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) over the past 6 months indicates strong household demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods when RSAFS has increased over the past 6 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3 percentage points from the prior month signals accelerating inflation, which prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3pp from prior month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both employment growth (PAYEMS) and labor force participation (UNRATE) indicate a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of periods when both PAYEMS and UNRATE decline from the prior month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high monetary policy rates (FEDFUNDS > 3.0%), the Federal Reserve is in a tightening cycle, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 3.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
